articleHeadlineTranslated: Is killing mosquitoes enough to prevent dengue fever?
articleHeadline: Đập chết muỗi có đủ để phòng sốt xuất huyết?
articleSummary: Killing mosquitoes alone is insufficient to prevent dengue fever in Vietnam, because after an infected person is bitten, Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus can lay eggs in water containers; eggs hatch within about 3 days into larvae that quickly become adults, allowing ongoing transmission even during insecticide campaigns. Eliminating larval habitats is essential—turn over water containers and remove standing water to prevent mosquitoes from laying eggs. Dengue remains a year-round burden in Vietnam: 2025 saw 184,903 cases—the highest in the Asia-Pacific region; in the first 10 months of 2026, 170,684 suspected cases and 21 deaths. Transmission involves an 8–12 day extrinsic incubation in mosquitoes. Symptoms begin with high fever; defervescence can trigger severe complications, including shock. Early medical care is vital, with warning signs such as persistent fever, fatigue, abdominal pain, and vomiting; high-risk groups include pregnant women, children, the elderly, and those with underlying conditions. Public advice: no-larvae, no dengue.
notes: 記事はベトナムの年次デング熱状況（2025年18万件超、2026年1-10月で17万件・死亡21人）に言及しているが、これは例年と同水準の季節性流行であり、新規性・異常性は認められない。中国は発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及なし。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Can Hepatitis B virus be transmitted through saliva?
articleHeadline: Viêm gan virus B có lây qua đường nước bọt?
articleSummary: HBV is an infectious disease caused by the hepatitis B virus that can survive outside the body for at least 7 days. Transmission occurs mainly through mother-to-child, blood exposure, and unsafe sexual contact, with spread possible when blood or body fluids contact mucous membranes or open wounds. Do not share items that can contain blood—razors, shaving blades, toothbrushes, or nail clippers. The virus can be present in saliva but is not easily transmitted by ordinary contact; the US CDC states HBV does not spread via food, shared meals, coughing, sneezing, or kissing. Family members should get tested; susceptible individuals should discuss vaccination. People with HBV should follow medical guidance, avoid sharing blood-containing items, use condoms if a partner’s immune status is unknown, and cover bleeding wounds; do not donate blood. Authored by ThS.BS Pham Khac Khiem, Hanoi Tam Anh General Hospital.

articleHeadline: SARS-CoV-2 Exposure Triggers Abnormal Immune Cell Growth and T Cell Loss
articleSummary: SARS-CoV-2 exposure triggers imbalanced immune responses in lymphoid tissues, with excessive plasma cell development and marked T cell depletion observed in lymph nodes from COVID-19 decedents in China. Abstract published in Frontiers in Immunology.

articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues, with spillover toward Kenya and Nigeria. No vaccine is licensed for Bundibugyo or Sudan strains; Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) is licensed only for Zaire and cannot be assumed protective against Bundibugyo. A study led by Leonie Mayer (DZIF) and Hamburg-Eppendorf found Ervebo can trigger T-cell responses to Bundibugyo and, to a lesser extent, Sudan, implying cross-recognition but not proven protection. Authorities warn that vaccination without demonstrated efficacy may create unsafe complacency and undermine trust. Since May, as of Oct 25, the DRC has reported over 10,000 Bundibugyo infections, with 4,887 deaths (case fatality ~48.6%), and transmission is hampered by conflict, disrupted transport, attacks on health facilities, and weak surveillance. The Tumaini program in DRC advances Oxford and Moderna vaccine candidates; robust efficacy data are months away, possibly mid-2027, while a pan-Ebola vaccine remains a long-term aim; urgent Bundibugyo-focused vaccines are prioritized.

articleSummary: Brazil is expanding release of Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti to curb dengue. Currently 16 municipalities participate; 54 more cities are planned by 2027 with 117 million reais. The approach began in Jurujuba, Niterói (RJ) between Aug 2015 and Jan 2016, reaching the city by 2019. Fiocruz pilots showed dengue cases fell 69% after two years and ~90% after five. Eggs are produced at two biofactories—Wolbito Brasil in Curitiba (up to 150 million/week) and Flyttr in Campinas (up to 190 million)—with weekly releases. Wolbachia-carrying offspring spread; in some weeks ~70% of local mosquitoes become carriers, reducing transmission. Establishment takes about 26 weeks. The method was formalized in Brazil’s national dengue plan in 2024. Dengue reached its worst year since 2000 with 6.56 million cases and 6,321 deaths; El Niño projections for 2026–27 predict large regional increases. Regulatory and budget hurdles remain; Flyttr offers wAlbB, a heat-tolerant strain, as a potential option.

articleSummary: Leishmaniasis, transmitted by sandflies, is discussed by a Humap-UFMS specialist. Sandflies are most active in late afternoon and at night. The cutaneous form typically affects exposed skin—arms, legs, and face—forming a round lesion with raised borders that rarely hurts; without proper care it can persist for months and leave scars. The incubation period ranges from weeks to months; patients may return from transmission areas and develop symptoms later. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment and laboratory tests; treatment is free through SUS. Prevention emphasizes vector control: repellents, screens, long clothing, and environmental cleaning.

Five agents account for most cases: Helicobacter pylori with about 760,000 cancers (roughly 4%), HPV causing about 750,000 cancers (primarily cervical cancer), HBV ≈360,000, HCV ≈160,000, and EBV ≈260,000. Of HPV, types 16 and 18 underlie about three-quarters of HPV-attributable cancers. Regionally, infection-related cancers hit low- and middle-income countries hardest (about 77%). East Asia bears high burdens from H. pylori and HBV; Africa south of the Sahara has the highest proportional share due to HPV. In Western Europe ~5% of new cancers in 2024 are infection-associated; Germany reported 29,000 such cancers (HPV ~11,000; H. pylori ~9,700). Thirteen pathogens are classed as carcinogenic (9 viruses, 1 bacterium, 3 parasites: Opisthorchis viverrini, Clonorchis sinensis, Schistosoma haematobium). Plasmodium falciparum’s link to Burkitt lymphoma is deemed probable.

articleHeadline: Novel KLUS Enzyme Subgroup Identified in CTX-M Family
articleSummary: Hangzhou CDC and Chinese CDC researchers identified a novel KLUS subgroup of CTX-M-type extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) in China, expanding CTX-M diversity; findings published in Frontiers in Microbiology (2026). Structural modeling shows 11 α-helices, 5 β-sheets, conserved catalytic cavity and SDN loop, and 23 substitutions vs CTX-M-2, including V77I near the Ω-loop. articleHeadline: Molecular Testing Detects Urogenital Pathogens in Women With
articleSummary: At Minhang Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, a retrospective case-control study (June–September 2025) of 309 women evaluated 155 symptomatic vaginitis patients with negative wet-mount/Gram results (Nugent 0–3) and 154 asymptomatic controls (Nugent 0). A positive non-Ureaplasma result occurred in 61/155 symptomatic (39.4%) vs 23/154 controls (14.9%), age-adjusted OR 3.60 (95% CI 2.12–6.30; p<0.001). Trichomonas vaginalis was detected in 36/155 symptomatic but in 0/154 controls (OR 110.16; 95% CI 15.08–14,046.89; p<0.001; remains significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction). Chlamydia trachomatis (11 vs 3) and Candida glabrata (5 vs 0) showed nominal associations with small counts; Ureaplasma parvum showed inverse nominal association. Normalized Ureaplasma loads did not differ between groups. Authors conclude non-Ureaplasma targets are more prevalent in microscopy-negative symptomatic women and molecular testing could complement routine diagnostics, but DNA detection alone cannot establish viability or causality; larger prospective studies are needed.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Was humanity's oldest plague outbreak in Siberia 5,500 years ago? The key to unraveling history is the marmot, a familiar creature that serves as the vector.

articleSummary: Oldest human plague outbreak occurred around Lake Baikal in SE Siberia about 5,500 years ago, with evidence in hunter-gatherer burials of Yersinia pestis and the Siberian marmot Marmota sibirica as the likely reservoir. Archaeological finds include hundreds of marmot incisors buried with the dead, suggesting close human-marmot interaction. Later outbreaks linked to marmots include the 1910–1911 Manchuria plague with roughly 60,000 deaths. In Mongolia and regional Manchuria, marmot hunting remains culturally important; in 2019 a Mongolian couple died after eating marmot viscera raw, and in 2020 a 15-year-old hunter died after a marmot encounter. Marmots support long-term plague persistence; fleas transfer the bacterium between marmots and to humans. Baikal-era strains lacked ymT, but ~3,800-year-old strains carried it, enabling broader flea transmission. Soviet eradication efforts failed; climate and landscape drive endemicity, underscoring the need to coexist with disease."

articleHeadline: Support Vector Machine Leads Prediction of Infection After Open Pulmonary
articleSummary: West China Hospital evaluated nine machine-learning models using 14 clinical variables to predict postoperative infection after open pulmonary lobectomy in 3,160 patients treated from 2017–2025; 369 infections occurred (11.68%). Calibration varied (Brier 0.156–0.241). Decision-curve analysis showed net benefit at low thresholds (0.01–0.11). SHAP highlighted age, total surgical duration, and preoperative hospital stay as key predictors across models. Conclusion: ML risk stratification using pre/intraoperative data shows potential and warrants external validation.

articleSummary: Retrospective analysis of Ni-kshay records from Maharashtra, India, 2021–2022 identified predictors of adverse outcomes in adult drug-sensitive TB.
